title: Forward-only migrations with named reverts and a live schema-version report
iWant: every migration to know how to undo itself and every instance to report what schema it runs
soThat: deploys are ordered, reversible on purpose, and verifiable from the outside

acceptanceCriteria.description: Migrations apply strictly forward in a deterministic order; the tool refuses to apply migrations out of order or to skip gaps.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a migration set with an out-of-order or missing member
acceptanceCriteria.then: the tool refuses with an error naming the ordering violation

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every migration ships a named revert step, and the revert is exercised at least once in verification (apply then revert restores the prior schema).
acceptanceCriteria.when: it is applied and its named revert executed
acceptanceCriteria.then: the schema returns to its prior state

acceptanceCriteria.description: The deploy order between migrations and application rollout is stated in the project documentation, including which schema versions each application version tolerates.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the migration-versus-rollout order is looked up
acceptanceCriteria.then: the order and the tolerated schema-version window are stated

acceptanceCriteria.description: GET /v1/_meta returns the current schema version and application version against a declared schema, under the same wire contract as every other endpoint.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response conforms to the declared meta schema carrying schema version and application version

acceptanceCriteria.description: The schema version reported by /v1/_meta equals the version recorded by the migration tool in the database, so the endpoint reports reality rather than a build-time constant.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an instance after applying a new migration
acceptanceCriteria.when: /v1/_meta and the migration tool's recorded version are compared
acceptanceCriteria.then: they are equal, and change together when the next migration applies

acceptanceCriteria.description: The /v1/_meta endpoint declares an auth class like any other endpoint (service or admin by default), and startup readiness (AC-2108-4) gates on migrations being current.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the generated spec and a booting instance behind on migrations
acceptanceCriteria.when: the _meta declaration and the startup probe are inspected
acceptanceCriteria.then: _meta carries its declared auth class, and the startup probe withholds 200 until migrations are current
